hints: Notice the table asks for two different quantities - mass is measured in $\text{kg}$ while weight is a force measured in $\text{N}$.
Recall that in $F = ma$ the mass $m$ controls how much acceleration a given force produces, which is inertia or resistance to acceleration.
Recall that weight on Earth is given by $W = mg$ and acts as the gravitational pull of the Earth on the object.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the physical meaning of mass versus the physical meaning of weight on the Earth.
State the rule for mass: from Newton's second law $F = ma$, mass is the measure of inertia, the property that resists acceleration.
State the rule for weight: weight is a force due to gravity, $W = mg$, equal to the pull of the Earth on the object.
Check the tempting errors: momentum divided by velocity and work in lifting one metre give correct numbers in special cases but are not definitions, and mass divided by $g$ has the wrong algebra.
Combine both correct meanings: mass as resistance to acceleration paired with weight as pull of the Earth. This is option D.

options.A: Although $p/v$ equals mass numerically, it is not the meaning of mass, and work done lifting one metre equals $W \times 1 \text{ m}$ which is an energy, not the force weight.
options.B: The descriptions are swapped - the gravitational force on it is weight, while the property that resists acceleration is inertia or mass.
options.C: The pull of the Earth is weight not mass, and weight is $W = mg$ so mass multiplied by acceleration of free fall, not divided by it.
options.D: Mass measures inertia, the resistance to acceleration in $F = ma$, and weight is the gravitational pull of the Earth, $W = mg$.
